newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish GDP rises 6.0 pct in 96, seen maybe slowing.
newsitem.headline: Polish GDP rises 6.0 pct in 96, seen maybe slowing.

text.p: Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) growth slowed to six percent last year from seven percent in 1995 and may slow further this year, the president of the Central Statistial Office (GUS) said on Thursday.
Tadeusz Toczynski told a news conference the 1996 growth was fuelled by a jump in domestic demand which replaced exports as the main engine of Poland's growth.
"Last year's GDP rise was mainly fuelled by a strong growth of domestic demand," a GUS report presented by Toczynski said.
"It was slower than in 1995 due to slower growth of gross added value in industrial production, in the construction and agriculture sectors...because of a harsh winter," it said.
According to preliminary GUS data consumption in 1996 rose 7.2 percent against a 4.1 percent rise in 1995 and investment rose 21.6 percent against 18.5 percent in 1995.

Gross added value in industry rose 7.7 percent in 1996 against a 9.9 percent rise in 1995. It rose 3.9 percent in construction against 7.3 percent and 4.7 percent in agriculture against 11.6 percent in 1995.

Toczynski said the high internal demand of 1996 was not likely to be sustainable in 1997 because much of it was created by a boom in credit for households and a drop in savings, which was likely to be curbed this year.

He also expected problems in bringing down unemployment and with the implementation of social security system reform -- factors which he said could slow Poland's growth in a year of parliamenytary elections.
"The government believes that 1997 is going to be a good year, and some even say it may be the best one since the start of market reforms in 1989," Toczynski said.

"It will be difficult to maintain such a fast rate of GDP growth this year because the dynamics of consumption may fall, unemployment will not drop as fast as in 1996...and we still face the difficult social security reform," he said.
Poland's unemployment rate fell to 13.6 percent in December 1996 from 14.9 percfent in December 1995.
Toczynski said the GDP data was preliminary and GUS will release revised 1996 figures in March.
"Howver, they should not differ from the preliminary data by 0.1-0.2 point," he said.
In 1997 GUS will also release quarterly GDP data two months after the end of each quarter.
